meta.title: ACCT 321 — Worked Example Set 1: Service Business — Month 1
meta.description: A new sole proprietorship service business. All transactions are cash-based. Students practice basic journal entries for a service company.
learning_objectives: Record owner investment in the business
Record cash purchases of assets and expenses

transactions.description: On January 1, John Smith invested $50,000 cash to start a consulting business, Smith Consulting.
transactions.explanation: The owner's cash investment increases both the asset Cash (debit) and the equity account Owner's Capital (credit). This is the fundamental accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. Cash (asset) increases by $50,000, and Owner's Capital (equity) increases by $50,000.

transactions.description: On January 3, purchased office supplies for $800 cash.
transactions.explanation: Supplies is an asset account. When supplies are purchased, the asset Supplies increases (debit) and Cash decreases (credit). Note: Supplies is not an expense at purchase — it becomes an expense only when consumed.

transactions.description: On January 5, purchased office equipment for $3,000 cash.
transactions.explanation: Equipment is a long-term asset. The purchase increases Equipment (debit) and decreases Cash (credit). Equipment will be depreciated over its useful life, but we record the purchase at cost first.

transactions.description: On January 10, earned $2,500 cash for consulting services provided to a client.
transactions.explanation: Revenue increases equity. Cash increases (debit) because the business received cash, and Service Revenue increases (credit). Revenue accounts have a normal credit balance because they increase equity.

transactions.description: On January 12, paid $1,200 cash for January office rent.
transactions.explanation: Rent is an expense of the current period. Expenses decrease equity, so Rent Expense increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Expenses always have a normal debit balance.

transactions.description: On January 15, earned $3,000 cash for consulting services provided to another client.
transactions.explanation: Same pattern as transaction 4. Cash increases (debit) and Service Revenue increases (credit). Each revenue transaction is recorded separately to maintain a clear audit trail.

transactions.description: On January 20, paid $600 cash for employee salaries.
transactions.explanation: Salaries are an operating expense. Salaries Expense increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Salaries are recorded when paid, not when earned by employees (cash basis for simplicity in this example).

transactions.description: On January 25, paid $150 cash for utilities (electricity and internet).
transactions.explanation: Utilities Expense increases with a debit, and Cash decreases with a credit. Like all expenses, utilities reduce the owner's equity.

transactions.description: On January 28, John Smith withdrew $1,000 cash for personal use.
transactions.explanation: Owner's Drawings is a contra-equity account (normal debit balance). It represents the owner taking assets out of the business for personal use. Drawings decrease equity, so they are recorded with a debit. This is NOT an expense — it is a distribution of profits.

transactions.description: On January 31, earned $1,800 cash for consulting services provided to a client.
transactions.explanation: Final revenue transaction of the month. Cash increases (debit) and Service Revenue increases (credit). Total revenue for the month: $2,500 + $3,000 + $1,800 = $7,300.

key_takeaways: Every transaction has equal debits and credits
Assets increase with debits, decrease with credits
Liabilities and Equity increase with credits, decrease with debits
Expenses and Drawings decrease equity (debit balance)
Owner's Capital is credited for investments, Owner's Drawings is debited for withdrawals
